description: The chart presents the distribution of problem correctness under two settings: with knowledge (w/ knowledge) and without knowledge (w/o knowledge), using Chain of Thought (CoT) reasoning. It is divided into three categories: easy, medium, and hard problems. In the easy category, the majority of problems are hindered by a lack of knowledge, with N−K+ accounting for approximately 50%. The medium category shows a consistent dominance of reasoning-based errors, with N−K− making up 15%. In the hard category, the primary bottleneck is the inability to integrate geometric reasoning, as indicated by the sharp decline in N+K+ to below 10%. The chart includes a legend with color coding for each category: N+K+ (green), N−K+ (yellow), N−K− (orange), and N+K− (red). The percentages are displayed inside the corresponding slices for each category.
